information_for_contributors: A modest PlantUML grammar: enough to read a diagram at a glance, not an
attempt to parse a language that has no published grammar and roughly
thirty dialects behind @startuml, @startmindmap, @startgantt, @startsalt …
Three things are worth knowing before editing it.
1. TextMate resolves overlaps by LEFTMOST match, and only breaks ties by
the order patterns are listed. So `"a -> b"` highlights as a string —
the quote is at a lower index than the arrow — no matter where the two
rules sit in the list below. The order in `patterns` is therefore
readability first, with ties (all the line-anchored rules start at the
same index) arranged most specific to most general.
2. The apostrophe comment is anchored to the start of a line. PlantUML's
documentation says a `'` begins a comment, and every other PlantUML
grammar takes that literally with `'.*$` — which then eats the rest of
`Alice -> Bob : don't panic` and paints half the file as a comment.
Anchoring costs a trailing-comment idiom nobody uses and buys back every
English contraction in every label.
3. Most keyword rules are anchored to the start of a line too, and the ones
that are not have had the English-looking words taken out of them. Every
PlantUML keyword except `as`, `is`, `then`, `extends` and `implements`
heads a statement, whereas the busiest line in any sequence diagram is
`Alice -> Bob : some ordinary prose` — and that prose is full of words
like `file`, `state`, `node`, `left` and `over`. Unanchored keywords
turn every message into a light show. Where prose can be identified —
a note body, a title, an activity action — it is captured as a string,
which also stops anything inside it being matched further.
There is deliberately no `$schema` key: it makes VS Code fetch a schema
over the network when this file is opened, and this family's whole point
is that nothing reaches for the network.
The scope name must stay `source.plantuml` — package.json's `grammars`
entry and the fenced-block injection both name it.
name: PlantUML

patterns.comment: Block comment. Listed before the line comment so that a `/'` opening a block wins over the `'` inside it; in practice they never tie, because the block starts one character earlier.
patterns.name: comment.block.plantuml

patterns.comment: Line comment — only at the start of a line. See note 2 in the header: an unanchored `'` swallows apostrophes in labels.

diagram-markers.comment: @startuml/@enduml and the two dozen sibling pairs (@startmindmap, @startgantt, @startsalt, @startjson, @startwbs, …). Matched by shape rather than from a list, because PlantUML keeps adding them and a stale list silently stops highlighting a new diagram type.

patterns.comment: The file-pulling directives get their argument scoped as a string, chiefly so that `!include ../shared.puml` does not light its `..` up as a dotted arrow.

notes.comment: Notes come in three shapes and only one of them is a block. `note left : text` ends on its own line; `note "text" as N1` is a whole declaration; `note over A, B` opens a block that runs to `end note`. The block rule therefore refuses any line carrying a colon or a quotation mark, or it would swallow the rest of the diagram looking for an `end note` that was never going to come.

patterns.comment: Single-line form. The target clause (`left of Bob`, `over A, B`) is left unscoped on purpose: it is a capture, so nothing inside it can be matched further, and painting `right` as a keyword there would be noise.
Multi-line form. The body is scoped as a string so that the extent of the note is visible at a glance — which is most of the reason to highlight a note at all.
patterns.name: meta.note.plantuml

captions.comment: title / header / footer / caption / legend, each written either inline or as a block closed by `end <keyword>`. Capturing the text as a string is not decoration: without it a title such as `Left to right — the fork` lights up `left`, `right` and `fork` as keywords.

patterns.comment: Block form: the keyword, an optional position, and nothing else on the line.
patterns.name: meta.caption.plantuml

patterns.comment: Inline form. `newpage` joins them here because its optional argument is a title too.

activity.comment: An activity-diagram action: `:do the thing;`. The body is prose and is scoped as a string for the same reason a note body is. An action always carries a terminator (`;` `|` `<` `>` `]` `}` `/`) — it is required syntax, not a convention — so the block reliably closes.
activity.name: meta.activity.plantuml

declarations.comment: A declaration at the head of a line, so that the thing being named reads as a name. The full noun list is safe here precisely because it is anchored — a message line never begins with `file` or `state`. A quoted name (`participant "Long Name" as B`) is left to the string rule: capture 3 simply does not match, the rule stops after the keyword, and the scanner picks the string up one character later.

patterns.comment: Ends at the closing quote or, failing that, at the end of the line: PlantUML strings are single-line (a line break inside one is written `\n`), and an unterminated quote must not paint the remainder of the file.
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.plantuml

stereotypes.comment: `<<interface>>`, `<<(A,#FF7700)>>`. The negative lookahead keeps this off the sequence-diagram arrow `A <<-- B`, whose `<<` is followed by line characters rather than by a stereotype name.

comment: The relation operator, in four alternatives. Read them as: (1) something
decorated on the left — `<|--`, `*--`, `o--`, `}o--`; (2) something
decorated on the right — `-->`, `..|>`, `--*`, `->>`; (3) an undecorated
line carrying a modifier or a direction — `-[#red]-`, `-down-`; (4) a
plain run of two or more line characters — `--`, `..`, `==`.
At least one of those conditions must hold, which is what keeps the rule
off ordinary hyphens: a single `-` with nothing attached is not an arrow.
`o` and `x` are arrowheads (`A o-- B`, `A ->x B`) and also perfectly
ordinary letters, so each carries a word-boundary guard. Without the
lookbehind, the `x-` of a node named `box-1` reads as a lost-message
arrow. The `>` and `|` heads need no such guard, which matters because
`A -->Bob` is legal and must not be broken by one.
The `\` and `/` half-arrows (`A -\ B`, `A //-- B`) are deliberately
absent: `//` also opens creole italics, and mistaking emphasis for an
arrow is worse than missing a rare arrow.
A colour modifier written inside an arrow (`-[#red]->`) is swallowed by
the arrow scope rather than picked out as a colour. That is the price of
matching the operator as one token, and one token is what it is.
Each decoration slot repeats up to twice, which is what entity-relation
diagrams need: crow's-foot notation stacks two of them a side, as in
arrows.name: keyword.operator.arrow.plantuml

patterns.comment: #RGB, #RGBA, #RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB. Longest alternative first, so `#AABBCC` is one colour and not `#AAB` followed by rubble.
patterns.name: constant.other.color.plantuml

patterns.comment: A named colour, but only where a name can only be a colour — after `[`, `,`, `:` or `=`. A bare `#name` is left alone on purpose: inside a class body `#field` means a protected member, and painting every protected member as a colour would be wrong more often than it is right.
patterns.name: constant.other.color.plantuml

patterns.comment: Flow control. Anchored: every one of these words heads a statement, and every one of them is also ordinary English that turns up in message text.
patterns.name: keyword.control.plantuml

patterns.comment: Directives. Anchored for the same reason.
patterns.name: keyword.other.plantuml

patterns.comment: The five words that genuinely occur mid-line, in `Alice as A`, `Foo extends Bar`, `if (x) then (yes)`.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.word.plantuml

patterns.comment: The declaration nouns, unanchored so that `Foo <|-- class Bar` still reads. Trimmed to the eight that are never mistaken for prose — `file`, `node`, `state`, `card`, `control` and the rest of the list stay in `declarations`, where the line anchor protects them.
patterns.name: storage.type.plantuml

variables.comment: Preprocessor variables, `$name`, and sprite references such as `<$aws>`.
variables.name: variable.other.plantuml
